messages:
sam: noticed a burst of interservice TLS failures in ap-south and eu-west starting 2026-05-10T11:04Z. Symptoms: 'tls: write alert: internal error' and occasional client cert rejects
rita: stack traces point to keystore unwrap 403s at the same times. KMS audit shows alternating Allow/Deny for the same key and principal depending on which auth controller answered the request
chen: logs (redacted):
```
proxy[edge-9]: 2026-05-10T11:04:12Z error: tls: write alert: internal error svc=ingress-ap-south client=svc-account:worker-ap
rotator[keystore]: 2026-05-10T11:04:12Z error: unwrap failed key=projects/redwood/keys/serving-main err=403 KMSDecryptDenied principal=svc-account:worker-ap
```
lina: audit shows an RBAC change and an infra "deny:keystore:unwrap" policy deployed within the same minute. The deny has higher precedence in the policy engine, but one control-plane replica still had the old bindings for a brief window causing inconsistent decisions
oncall: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) apply explicit allow RoleBinding for critical runtime SAs in affected namespaces 2) re-enable local rotator cache TTL=45s 3) set temporary KMS grant for key with 1h expiry to cover windows during RBAC reconciliation
sam: applying allow for worker-ap and ingress-ap now (kubectl apply rolebinding...), switching rotator back to TTL=45s
sec-bot: automated-alert: keystore-decrypt-errors spike detected 2026-05-10T11:06Z. incident INC-188888 opened
rita: enabled decision-level audit for keystore and queued a targeted query for the conflicting policy IDs; will share the decision_id list here once available
chen: follow-ups: 1) require RBAC preflight: run a canary unwind test that performs unwraps from every region before merge 2) add a deploy check that denies precedence flips without canary 3) document rotator cache as required during alias flips 4) add CI matrix test for TLS negotiation + unwrap during alias rotation
lina: created ticket SEC-2026-244, assigned infra+platform. I'll own the writeup once oncall confirms stable for 1h
oncall: metrics look stable; handshake failures back to baseline ~8m after fixes. keeping temporary grants for 1h and leaving rotator TTL at 45s until alias reconciliation completed
sam: thanks all. will include decision_ids and audit snippets in the final blameless summary. :heart:
